clue.text: Black plant for wealthy globetrotters?

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black, as in jet-black hair
a set is a young plant or bulb ready for planting, as in onion sets

explanation.surface: A dark-leaved shrub is somehow recommended as a gift for rich travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' and 'plant' look like one item, a dark plant, but each gives a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the fashionable rich who fly from resort to resort, hence the question mark on a playful description.

clue.text: Bonus having girl, 6, with daughter around study?

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
VI is 6 in Roman numerals
a den is a private study or workroom
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A father wonders whether a bonus covers a six-year-old girl and her sister studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is loose: the daughter's letter does not enclose the study but sits beside it, at its end, so the last four letters run study then daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dividend is a share of profits paid out, an extra sum received, so it is a kind of bonus.

clue.text: Brutish chap we let tiro stupidly start to respect

indicators.note: doing something stupidly suggests a muddle, so these letters are jumbled into a new order
the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from respect

explanation.surface: A novice is told off for letting a thuggish man in without showing any respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges WE LET TIRO into ROTTWEILE, and 'start to' adds the R of 'respect'. A tiro is a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is borrowed from the aggressive guard-dog breed to describe a bullying, thuggish man.

clue.text: Noted Croat sadly stripped of new academic honour

indicators.note: something done sadly goes wrong, so these letters are put out of order
being stripped of something means losing it, so one letter is removed

explanation.surface: A distinguished Croatian academic is unhappily deprived of a fresh university award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges NOTED CROAT, and 'stripped of' takes the N (new) out of that pool, leaving the nine letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate is the highest university degree, an honour conferred on a scholar.

clue.text: Cheesy stuff from Asian, we hear

indicators.note: we hear points to a word that sounds like the one given, not one spelt like it

parts.note: a Kurd is a person from Kurdistan, a region of western Asia

explanation.surface: Someone claims a dairy product comes from an Asian supplier, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns KURD, a member of the Asian people, into a word said the same way but spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Curds are the solid lumps formed when milk sours, the raw material of cheese.

clue.text: Ambassador left satisfied gaining capital protection

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE
to have met a demand is to have satisfied it

explanation.surface: A diplomat departs content after winning protection for the nation's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' here means of the head, not a city: the definition describes headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital in the old sense relates to the head, and a helmet is armour worn on the head.

clue.text: Conventional rallying point

explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal or usual; it is also a flag carried in battle around which troops gather.

clue.text: English book containing good summary

indicators.note: containing means the first pieces hold another piece within them

parts.note: a tome is a large heavy book
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: An English volume that includes a positive summary of its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a condensed account giving the essence of a longer work, an abstract.

clue.text: BBC official in middle of week gets advantage

indicators.note: in places the official's letters inside the pair taken from the middle of week
the middle of a word is its central letters, here the inner pair of week

parts.note: the head of the BBC is the Director General, abbreviated DG

explanation.surface: A senior broadcasting executive gains an edge by turning up midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the inner pair of letters of 'week', and 'in' sets the official between them. The BBC is Britain's national public broadcaster; its chief is the Director General.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge over a rival means holding a slight superiority or lead.

clue.text: Rolling work curtailed fast

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially a musical composition
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A rolling programme of work is cut short so it can be completed quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the S from OPUS. 'Rolling' looks like a verb, but it is the informal sense, as in 'rolling in money'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rolling, in informal speech, means having lots of money, which matches lavish wealth.

clue.text: Close fitting? Good when in this knit woolly

indicators.note: in signals that one letter goes inside the rearranged letters
woolly means muddled or vague, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A knitter boasts that this woolly garment is good and fits snugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' rearranges THIS KNIT, and 'in' puts G among those letters; 'when' is a link. 'woolly' looks descriptive of a jumper, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that clings tightly to the body is fitting closely, the question mark marking the playful split phrase.

clue.text: March trailed by new energetic figure

indicators.note: trailed by means the second piece follows behind the first

parts.note: a demo is a protest march, short for demonstration

explanation.surface: A protest march followed by a fresh, lively spokesperson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but means a protest procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who works furiously hard is called a demon, as in 'a demon for work'.

clue.text: Recurrent idea from article by writer

parts.note: the is the definite article in grammar
the writer, from the setter's point of view, is me

explanation.surface: An essay's repeated notion is taken from a piece by an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is the setter referring to themself, giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif that keeps coming back in a work of music or writing is its main subject.

clue.text: Maritime event having at sea great set of volunteers

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the following word is rearranged

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's reserve force of part-time volunteer soldiers

explanation.surface: A big yachting meet with a fine crowd of willing helpers out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' sits naturally in the maritime picture, hiding its job as the anagram signal for 'great'; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat or yacht races held on water.

clue.text: Part of course by fellow in Switzerland for flighty creature

parts.note: a green is part of a golf course, the area around the hole
CH, for Confoederatio Helvetica, is Switzerland's international code

explanation.surface: A golfer on a Swiss links spots a skittish animal near the hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' is used literally: the creature flies.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common songbird of Europe, and as a bird it is a creature capable of flight.

clue.text: She departed in incendiary circumstances

parts.note: read as the death of a woman in a fire: the French saint and soldier burned at the stake at Rouen in 1431

explanation.definitionFit: The Maid of Orleans was executed by burning, so she literally died amid flames.

clue.text: Unexciting location dividing traffic?

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means moderate and bland; literally it is the centre line of a highway, between the two streams of vehicles.

clue.text: A mess with car crashing — and carnage!

indicators.note: a car crashing ends up wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A car pile-up causes chaos and bloodshed on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' rearranges A MESS CAR; 'with' is a link joining the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the slaughter of many people, a bloodbath.

clue.text: Bloomer made by old Greek hero

parts.note: Leander is the Greek youth who swam the Hellespont nightly to reach his lover Hero

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek warrior makes an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant. Leander was loved by Hero, so he is literally Hero's man.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is anything that flowers, and this Mediterranean shrub is known for its pink and white flowers.

clue.text: Fans for rioting in orange

indicators.note: rioting fans run wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Football supporters in orange shirts are causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' rearranges FANS FOR; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice from crocus stigmas gives its name to a deep yellow-orange colour.

clue.text: Overpaid executive given some grief at cathedral

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grossly overpaid boss gets some trouble at the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'given' into the definition, but 'Overpaid executive given' cannot stand for the answer; 'given' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for a wealthy, highly paid business boss, often criticised for excessive pay.

clue.text: Relative close to café in French place

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the name of the French city

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the last letter of café is taken

explanation.surface: A relation sits near a café in a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like 'near' but means the end of 'café', its final E; 'in' puts that E inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling's daughter is a family member, a kind of relation.

clue.text: Recruit bridge players with catalogue

parts.note: in bridge the four players are called North, South, East and West; East and North give E and N
a list is a catalogue of items

explanation.surface: A card club signs up new members using a register of bridge players.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are known by compass points, so any two of N, S, E and W can stand for them.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit someone, or to join up yourself, is to sign up, especially for the armed forces.

clue.text: Gust caused by missile?

explanation.definitionFit: A scud is a sudden blast of wind or driving cloud; Scud is also the name of a Soviet-made ballistic rocket.

clue.text: Reportedly, modify part of church

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than seen, one sounding like the word given

parts.note: to modify something is to alter it

explanation.surface: Plans to change part of a church building have been rumoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns ALTER (modify) into a word said the same but spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The communion table at the east end of a church is its holiest fixture.

clue.text: Learner swapping halves in sandwich

indicators.note: swapping halves means the front pair and back pair of letters change places

parts.note: a tiro is a beginner or learner

explanation.surface: A trainee has to switch over the two halves of a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping halves' turns TI-RO into RO-TI; 'in' is a link. The definition stretches a little: a roti is a flatbread, in the Caribbean a filled wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A roti is an unleavened flatbread; in Trinidad it is wrapped round curry as a filled snack like a wrap.

clue.text: Imaginary spillage of oil in fact

indicators.note: a spillage scatters things about, so the letters of the following words are scattered

explanation.surface: Reports of an oil spill turn out to be invented, in fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spillage of' rearranges OIL IN FACT, and 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made up for a story, not real, is invented rather than true.

clue.text: Priest accepting a nuclear facility

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A clergyman agrees to have an atomic power plant built in his parish.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is the core installation in which controlled atomic fission produces power.

clue.text: Titled woman of the French game

parts.note: du is French for of the
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A noblewoman is fond of the French board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the French' looks like a description of the game, but it means the French for 'of the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke's wife holds a noble rank, a peeress with a title.
